description: Cases for matching a result to an output and to a request. Each case gives the result (result, a JSON value; or result_text, the exact text of a result that a JSON value cannot carry; null when no result is held), the candidate output in hexadecimal (null when none is held), and the caller's expectations (an absent member is an expectation that was not supplied). verdict is requested-run-completed, output-agreement or not-established; a not-established case names the rule identifier, and every case names in decided_by the step of section 8 of semantic-validation.md that decides it. materials gives the bytes the digests were computed from. A result given as a JSON value stands for its serialization as UTF-8 text.

source-same-length.note: Another source of the same length holding the same row.

source-other-length.note: Another source of another length holding the same row.

schema-same-length.note: The same schema with two members in the other order.

schema-other-length.note: The same schema followed by a line feed.

policy-same-length.note: The same policy with its members in the other order.

policy-other-length.note: Another policy. The table has no exact-number column, so the output is the same.

output-same-length.note: Other bytes of the same length.

cases.name: stale run, no expectations
cases.note: The result is from an earlier run that happened to produce the same bytes. With no expectations this is all that can be said, and it is not evidence that request-0042 completed. Compare the case named stale run.

cases.name: mutation: one hexadecimal digit of output.sha256
status: refused, source not read
cases.note: A valid refusal with no source entry. The matcher stops at the status and does not look for the entry.

cases.name: result: ok without counts
cases.note: A result that is refused as a document establishes nothing, whatever digest it carries.

cases.name: result: refused with an output member
cases.note: The smuggled member carries the true digest and length of the candidate. The result is refused at O-03 and the member is never compared.

cases.name: result: refused with a malformed output member
cases.note: Presence is settled before content: result-member-unknown, not result-member-invalid.

cases.name: result: output digest in upper case
cases.note: A digest is lowercase. It is not folded and then compared.

cases.name: result: counts inconsistent
cases.note: One row and two nulls. Every digest matches; the result is still not a valid result.

cases.name: result: status key repeated
cases.note: A parser that keeps the last of two keys reads ok and one that keeps the first reads refused. A repeated key is refused before either is read.

cases.name: stale run
cases.note: A valid result of an earlier run, the same inputs and the same output bytes. Only the caller's own run identifier tells it from the run that was requested.

cases.name: run id differs in letter case
different source, identical output
cases.note: The result is for another source of the same length that holds the same row, so the output bytes are identical.

cases.name: policy length differs
cases.note: The result is for a policy that differs in exact_numbers. The table has no exact-number column, so the output bytes are identical.

cases.name: status: refused, all expectations
cases.note: Every binding the refusal carries equals its expectation. No verdict binds a refusal to a request.

cases.name: missing expectation: run_id
cases.note: The three expectations supplied all match and the output agrees. The verdict is neither requested-run-completed nor output-agreement.

cases.name: missing expectation: source
cases.note: The three expectations supplied all match and the output agrees. The verdict is neither requested-run-completed nor output-agreement.

cases.name: missing expectation: schema
cases.note: The three expectations supplied all match and the output agrees. The verdict is neither requested-run-completed nor output-agreement.

cases.name: missing expectation: policy
cases.note: The three expectations supplied all match and the output agrees. The verdict is neither requested-run-completed nor output-agreement.

cases.name: missing expectation: three supplied, one of them wrong
cases.note: A partial set is not checked as far as it goes: the run identifier differs and the rule is still expectations-incomplete.

cases.name: missing expectation: and no result
cases.note: Decided before the absence of a result is noticed.

cases.name: expectation: digest in upper case
cases.note: Not folded to lower case and compared.

cases.name: expectation: length past the largest count
expectation: run identifier with a space
expectation: empty run identifier
cases.note: Decided before the absence of a result is noticed.

cases.name: mutation: one hexadecimal digit of inputs.source.sha256
mutation: one hexadecimal digit of inputs.schema.sha256
mutation: one hexadecimal digit of inputs.policy.sha256
mutation: one hexadecimal digit of the expected source digest
mutation: inputs.policy.bytes off by one
cases.note: The digest is still the right one.

cases.name: mutation: expected source length off by one
mutation: output.bytes off by one
cases.note: Every binding matches and the digest is the right one.

cases.name: mutation: one hexadecimal digit of output.sha256, all expectations
order: run id and output both differ
cases.note: Bindings are judged before the output.

cases.name: order: source and policy both differ
result: refused with an output member, all expectations
cases.note: Every binding matches and the smuggled member describes the candidate exactly.

cases.name: extension restates the status
cases.note: Extensions take no part in matching. Deleting the member gives the same verdict.

cases.name: extension restates the run identifier
cases.note: A stale result cannot be bound to the request through extension content.

cases.name: result: extensions past the value bound
cases.note: An unknown namespace is ignored only within the bounds.

cases.name: another profile
cases.note: profile takes no part in matching. A consumer that requires a profile compares it itself.
